findings.issue: Cross-tenant reaction visibility: reactions SELECT policy allows all authenticated users to read reactions across all workspaces
findings.impact: Reaction data (emoji + user_id mappings) is visible across tenant boundaries. While low-sensitivity, this violates the strict tenant isolation model used by all other tables. Combined with other data points, it enables cross-tenant user activity correlation.
findings.fix: Scope reactions RLS to workspace membership via messages -> channels -> workspace_members join chain.
findings.scenario: User A in Workspace X can enumerate reactions on messages in Workspace Y by guessing message IDs, discovering user-emoji relationships across tenants.

findings.issue: Channel export endpoint fetches unbounded message data without pagination
findings.impact: GET /channels/:channelId/export loads ALL messages into memory and returns them as a single JSON/CSV response. Channels with >10K messages cause memory exhaustion on both server and client. No rate limiting or size cap on this endpoint.
findings.fix: Add pagination with max limit (e.g., 1000 per page), streaming response, or document-based export with chunking.
findings.scenario: A channel with 50K messages hit the export endpoint: API server allocates ~100MB+ for the response, Node.js hits memory limit, process crashes.

findings.issue: GDPR data export uses getSupabaseAdmin() bypassing RLS for data collection
findings.impact: GDPR export endpoint uses service_role key (admin client) to collect user data. While user_id is constrained to req.userId, this pattern centralizes data access authority. If a bug in user_id handling occurs, or if the endpoint is called before full authentication, other users' data could leak. Service_role key exposure amplifies this risk.
findings.fix: Use per-user Supabase client (req.supabase) where RLS policies enforce user scoping. Only fall back to admin client for auth.admin operations that require service_role.
